messages:
customer-ops: Hey team — new customer 'AcmePay' reports SSO failures right after they rotated IdP signing cert. They see 403 on login and our logs show 'Invalid SAML signature' + 'Recipient URL mismatch'. Can we triage?

maria-support: Thanks — can you paste the exact error they get in our logs and the IdP metadata URL?

customer-ops: Error snippet we captured: `SAML validation failed: Signature check failed (no matching key). Recipient mismatch: expected https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/acme, got https://acme-idp.example.com/sso/acs`

customer-ops: IdP metadata: https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata.xml (they rotated cert earlier today at 16:05 UTC)

idp-sync-bot: Automated note: fetched metadata https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata.xml at 2025-06-12T16:12:40Z. Found 2 <KeyDescriptor> entries: key1 (old, use=signing), key2 (new, use=signing). new-cert thumbprint: 3A:2F:...

ryan-oncall: @dev-tj can you check our key-selection logic? If the IdP has two signing keys we should accept signatures from either key, but logs say none matched. Also Recipient mismatch is odd — usually that's from ACS or proxy rewriting host/port. :eyes:

dev-tj: Looking. Quick checklist: 1) confirm SP entityID and ACS we return to the IdP; 2) confirm our ACS URL canonicalization (trailing slash, port, scheme) vs what IdP is sending as Recipient; 3) check if any proxy in front is rewriting Host header or path.

maria-support: Confirming we told them SP entityID = `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/metadata/acme` and ACS = `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/acme` (no trailing slash). They say their IdP is sending Recipient = `https://acme-idp.example.com/sso/acs` in SAML (looks wrong).

customer-ops: They shared a decoded SAMLResponse (redacted):
```
<saml:Assertion>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:SubjectConfirmation>
      <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://acme-idp.example.com/sso/acs"/>
    </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
  </saml:Subject>
  <ds:Signature>
    <!-- signature validated against new cert -->
  </ds:Signature>
</saml:Assertion>
```

dev-tj: That Recipient is definitely wrong — looks like their IdP is misconfigured to reflect their own ACS endpoint rather than our SP ACS. Two parallel issues: signature key selection and Recipient mismatch. For signature: our SAML library checks signature against metadata-supplied keys; ensure metadata fetch has latest cert and not cached older version. For Recipient: IdP must set the Recipient to the SP's ACS.

ryan-oncall: Can you ask the customer to re-run metadata fetch on their IdP console (pointing at our SP metadata URL) and confirm the SP entity/ACS values? Also ask them to dump the raw SAMLResponse (base64) we can decode to verify signature and Recipient headers.

maria-support: Sent to customer: "Please confirm the ACS/EntityID configured in your IdP console (screenshot ok). Also attach the raw base64 SAMLResponse for a failed attempt, and the IdP metadata URL."

customer-ops: Customer returned: they had an SP template set to 'custom' and accidentally left 'Use Local ACS' enabled which rewrites Recipient to their internal ACS. They disabled it but still get 'Invalid signature' intermittently.

idp-sync-bot: Note: our metadata fetcher polled https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata.xml every 5m. Last successful load was 2025-06-12T16:12:40Z; content-length changed at 16:05:01Z (post-rotation). Fingerprint now matches new-cert 3A:2F:...

dev-tj: If the new cert is in metadata and our poll has picked it up, signature mismatch might be because the SAML Response was signed with the old key (IdP rotated but some nodes still sign with old key) or the signature reference/algorithm changed. Ask for raw base64 SAMLResponse and full verification log from their IdP.

maria-support: Customer uploaded raw SAMLResponse (base64). I decoded and verified: signature validation fails against new cert, but verifies against old cert. Also there's a short TTL: they rotated cert at 16:05 but some of their saml-proxies still sign with old key until 16:10. So transient mismatch.

ryan-oncall: Action items: 1) Ask customer to drain or restart saml-proxies so they sign with the new key consistently. 2) For Recipient mismatch, confirm IdP config now points to our ACS (they disabled local ACS). 3) I'll open a short-lived fallback: accept signatures verifying against either key for 10 minutes if their rotation window is problematic — but need eng approval. @dev-tj can you approve?

dev-tj: Approve short fallback for rotation window: implement an acceptance window that checks both current and previous metadata keys for up to 15 minutes post-update. Will create a rollback-safe feature flag gated to account 'acme' only. ETA: 2 hours.

maria-support: Confirmed with customer: after restarting their saml-proxies and disabling local ACS they can login. They saw a few failures during the 5-minute rotation window but now stable. Customer very happy. :tada:

ryan-oncall: I'll keep the fallback flag ready and coordinate with eng if they need it during future rotations. Closing once we verify no more failures in 24h.

maria-support: Marking resolved for now. Adding notes to account 'acme' support file: idp cert rotation caused mixed-key signing during rollout + local ACS misconfiguration. Recommend rolling rotation with short TTL and test node restart.
